what must stay human stewardship (criticality, retention exceptions, ambiguous PII classification) vs what to automate

Reveal: what the gates cannot decide

sources.source: Dehghani — Data Mesh Principles and Logical Architecture

items.item: A governance model requires automated execution of decisions by the platform; Dehghani calls this federated computational governance.
The federation of domain and platform product owners creates a set of global rules applied to all data products and their interfaces.
Organizations which design systems are constrained to produce designs which are copies of their own communication structures (Datamation, April 1968).

Dehghani's fourth principle, quoted directly in this topic, is the same federated computational governance Chapter 3's own data-mesh topic introduced as a named concept — this topic is where that name gets a concrete, running mechanism (the registration gate) rather than staying a definition.

The registration gate's classification check reuses the same tier-and-category tag topic 4 defined, and its rejection of an untagged free-text column is the same false-negative failure mode topic 4 named first — a scanner that never saw the column, not a tagging error.

The automated half of this topic's decision split (a rule over an attribute) is exactly the tag-based policy topic 7 introduced as the alternative to enumerating roles — this topic shows that same tag-based rule applied at the point a table is admitted, not just at query time.

Central policy applied computationally, this topic's own first clause, is the same shift topic 8 made for row and column security: a rule a person used to apply by hand becomes something the engine (there) or the platform (here) enforces on every table without being asked again.

at.topic: Row/column security and dynamic masking in-engine
at.quote: enforce in the query engine, not the application

items.item: A table admitted by the registration gate becomes discoverable in the same catalog topic 10 built, and the technical-vs-business split that topic drew (what a crawler can see vs what a person must name) is the same split this topic draws between a rule over an attribute and a judgement only a steward can make.

The contract fields this topic's registration gate checks (id, version, owner) are a stand-in for what Chapter 11's own contract-enforcement-in-CI topic would otherwise check at commit time — logged as a declared gap rather than assumed, since no section 11.4 entry exists yet.

at.step: Reveal: the registration gate, schema and contract

items.item: Placing a check as a gate before a table can be read by anyone, rather than as a post-hoc scan after it is already discoverable, is the same gate-vs-scan distinction topic 12 drew for data itself — here applied to a table's own right to exist in the catalog at all.

at.quote: where checks run (in-pipeline gates vs post-hoc scans)

items.item: A registered table's lineage, once it starts moving data, reports itself through the same run/job/dataset event model topic 11 built — this topic composes that mechanism rather than repeating it, exactly as CHAPTER.md's own leaves-out line states.

at.topic: OpenLineage: events, facets and lineage graphs

items.item: The six-decision automate-vs-human split, run and asserted in examples.py, is the Outcomes line's own test case made concrete: three decisions resolve to a stated rule, three resolve to a named steward with a reason, and no decision sits in both categories.

at.step: Reveal: automate, or ask a person?

items.item: Conway's own 1968 sentence, quoted in full, draws a line this topic then crosses deliberately: the forward law is something that happens to an organization; the reverse is a choice a platform team can make about which team split to create in the first place.

The registration gate's bug (initially rejecting a non-personal column for having category: None, when only tier is required to be non-null) is a concrete instance of this chapter's own recurring theme: a check that is too strict produces a false rejection, the mirror image of topic 4's false negative from a check that is too permissive.
